deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is not a Riemann manuscript. It is page 7 of a printed Berlin University lecture catalogue (Verzeichniss der Vorlesungen), kept in the Riemann papers, presumably because it dates from his Berlin student years (1847–1849). The page continues the section 'Mathematische Wissenschaften' and begins 'Naturwissenschaften'.

Mathematics entries:
- Ohm: higher equations.
- Grüson: elements of differential and integral calculus.
- Joachimsthal: integral calculus.
- Dirksen: transformation of functions (public), differential calculus, and the elements of analytic geometry.
- Lejeune-Dirichlet: theory of numbers, four times weekly 2–3, privatim; plus 'Anwendung der Integralrechnung auf die Zahlenlehre' (analytic number theory), once weekly, public.
- Encke: spherical astronomy and history of astronomy.

Natural sciences entries:
- Physics: Dove (experimental physics, optics), Schubarth (experimental physics), Karsten (electricity, theoretical optics), A. Erman (terrestrial magnetism), Magnus (physics colloquia).
- Medicine: Schultz (medical climatology).
- Chemistry: Mitscherlich, H. Rose, Heintz, Rammelsberg, Wuttig, Turte.
- Natural history and zoology: Link, Lichtenstein, Troschel.

The page carries no derivations and no handwritten mathematics. The only manuscript traces are:
- the archival folio number '60' in pencil at the right margin;
- a faint, largely illegible pencil note in the left margin just above the heading 'Naturwissenschaften'.

For biography, the page is indirect evidence of the courses offered while Riemann studied in Berlin. Riemann is known to have attended Dirichlet's number-theory lectures and Dirichlet's course applying analysis/integration to number theory there. Whether the faint marginal pencil note is in his hand cannot be determined from the image.

results.what: Printed university lecture catalogue listing Dirichlet's courses on number theory and on the application of integral calculus to number theory, alongside other Berlin mathematics and science lectures
results.modern_name: Archival/biographical document (course listing); no mathematical content

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed lecture catalogue with no mathematics by Riemann. Its only value is biographical context: the Berlin courses of the late 1840s, including Dirichlet's, which Riemann is already known to have attended.
